answer: Coordination-delay graph (CDG): each agent is a vertex; a group action requires a shared transcript whose edges are signed handoffs. A mesa scheduler orders handoffs, and each edge must carry a sable proof—a VDF seeded by the prior edge. Thus an attacker forging N sybils into one quorum pays N−1 sequential VDF delays plus verification; solo agents pay nothing. Cost is linear wall-clock delay per coordination edge, so mass coordination becomes expensive without identity gating.
